verification: Each supplied source/input/output was executed with the qualified native candidate. This does not imply native execution inside the browser.
puzzleRule: Puzzles check the requested story order, not whether every different order is an invalid RF2 program.

puzzles.title: Remember, change, display
puzzles.instruction: First remember two points, then add three, then display the total.
puzzles.explanation: Introduce the name before changing or displaying it. The result is five.
puzzles.correctSource:
let points = 2
set points = points + 3
show points

puzzles.title: Choose before you speak
puzzles.instruction: Introduce points, open the condition, put Level up! in the true branch, and finish the other branch.
puzzles.explanation: The condition chooses a branch. else starts the alternative and end closes the whole condition.
puzzles.correctSource:
let points = 12
if points >= 10
 say "Level up!"
else
 say "Keep practising."
end

puzzles.title: Say it three times
puzzles.instruction: Open a three-turn repeat, put the message inside, then close the block.
puzzles.explanation: Only the lines inside repeat/end are repeated. This produces three separate Go! lines.

puzzles.title: Define, then use
puzzles.instruction: For this puzzle, write the complete twice definition first, then use it to display twice three.
puzzles.explanation: The function has one return expression. This puzzle asks for definition-first order; RF2 also supports forward calls, so a different order is not automatically an invalid language program.
puzzles.correctSource:
fn twice(n)
 return n * 2
end
show twice(3)

whyFast.title: What actually makes a program fast?
whyFast.lead: Doing the needed work with less waste. Short source by itself is not a speed measurement.

points.title: Choose the work
points.text: A better algorithm can avoid repeated work. Check that it still gives the required answer.

points.title: Choose the representation
points.text: Data layout, bounds and instructions affect cost. Measure the complete useful job, including setup and IO.

points.title: Compile and reuse
points.text: The full native compiler emits ARM64 programs. Dynamic Simple programs currently include a native engine, rather than specialized machine code for every statement.

points.title: Measure the right engine
points.text: Browser worker timings describe the reference worker. Native build/run numbers require a real local compiler/runtime measurement. A source line count or logical step count is not CPU time.

whyFast.limits: No universal speed, energy, actual AI-token or C/assembly superiority claim is established. Earlier launch-time ranges overlap; no win is claimed from them.

executionModes.title: Reference worker
executionModes.meaning: Runs the browser-qualified reference engine with visible source/input/limits. Its trace is not native machine stepping.

executionModes.title: Native local
executionModes.meaning: Requires an explicitly selected loopback native bridge and actual native receipts. Never expose a public native POST endpoint to arbitrary source.
